hypotheses.title: Trielaidin Shortens Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: We hypothesize that trielaidin shortens lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. Exposure to this compound will reduce mean and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Trielaidin is an unnatural trans triglyceride that may disrupt membrane composition and lipid metabolism. Such disruption can impair cellular homeostasis and accelerate aging.
hypotheses.prediction: Animals treated with trielaidin will show a statistically significant reduction in lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Age-synchronize wild-type worms, treat one cohort with trielaidin and one with vehicle, and score survival daily. Compare lifespan distributions using log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Rapamycin Extends Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: We hypothesize that rapamycin extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. Exposure to this compound will increase mean and maximum lifespan relative to untreated controls.
hypotheses.rationale: Rapamycin inhibits the mTOR pathway, a central regulator of growth and nutrient sensing. Reduced mTOR signaling is expected to slow aging and prolong survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Animals treated with rapamycin will show a statistically significant increase in lifespan compared with vehicle-treated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Age-synchronize wild-type worms, treat one cohort with rapamycin and one with vehicle, and score survival daily. Compare lifespan distributions using log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Developmental Rapamycin Exposure Extends C. elegans Lifespan
hypotheses.claim: We hypothesize that rapamycin extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans only when administered during development. Exposure restricted to adulthood will not increase lifespan relative to controls.
hypotheses.rationale: mTOR signaling during development sets long-lasting metabolic and growth programs that influence aging. Interrupting these programs after development is complete may not alter lifespan.
hypotheses.prediction: Worms exposed to rapamycin during development will live significantly longer than controls, whereas worms exposed only during adulthood will not.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat age-synchronized worms with rapamycin during development only, adulthood only, or continuously, alongside vehicle controls. Score survival daily and compare all groups by log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Trielaidin Extends Lifespan via DAF-2 Activation
hypotheses.claim: We hypothesize that trielaidin extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by activating the insulin/IGF-1 receptor DAF-2 to reduce DAF-16 nuclear localization. This signaling change will mediate the longevity effect of the compound.
hypotheses.rationale: DAF-2 signaling negatively regulates the FOXO transcription factor DAF-16, a major determinant of longevity. Reduced DAF-16 nuclear activity can reprogram metabolism in a lifespan-extending manner.
hypotheses.prediction: Trielaidin-treated worms will show reduced DAF-16 nuclear localization, and the lifespan extension will be abolished in daf-2 or daf-16 loss-of-function backgrounds.
hypotheses.experiment: Treat DAF-16::GFP worms with trielaidin or vehicle and quantify nuclear DAF-16 fluorescence. In parallel, measure lifespan of trielaidin-treated daf-2 and daf-16 mutants versus wild type.
